newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa seeks better cost control.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa seeks better cost control.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG will seek to reduce its unit costs by 20 per cent by transferring some of its work, such as administration, to countries outside Germany, chairman Juergen Weber told a freight managers congress.

The airline is seeking savings of more than one billion marks in passenger operations by the year 2001, Weber said in a speech to the annual congress of the Germany Shippers Association (BVL) in Berlin.

This included the transfer of work to countries where equal competence and high quality standards exist at a fraction of the cost in Germany, such as the relocation of ticket billing to India, he said.
"The improvement of the costs side remains a permanent task of the management since our competitors are also following this path strongly," he said.

Weber did not give details of any forthcoming savings measures in his speech but cited the "drastic" analysis of American economist Lester Thurow on the consequences of globalisation for workers in industrial nations.

"The times are past in which first world wages can be paid in first world countries for jobs which are really for the third world. In future, third world products will be paid with third world wages, even if those who make them live in the first world," Weber quoted the economist as saying.

Companies such as Lufthansa had to adapt from simply providing transport services since these could be substituted more cheaply by carriers from countries with different pay and social structures to Germany, he noted.
